assessment.verifiedEvidence: Checked the official figure (20240526_co_second_q01.pdf, Q9) against official answer ハ. The question text, the four choices, and the figure all match: main-line B, B-H 10A, and two B-M 20A branches whose B symbols have a vertical line. The q9.png crop matches the figure. Legal basis: https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/safety_security/industrial_safety/sangyo/electric/files/20231226-2.pdf. WebFetch returned 403, so I used the attached SHA-pinned excerpt (PDF p.147). Article 148(1)(ii)(a): motor currents total 40A, which is at most 50A and larger than 10A, so I_W = 1.25×40 + 10 = 60A. Article 148(1)(v)(a): 3×40 + 10 = 130A. Item (b): the 2.5×I_W = 150A cap does not apply, because 130A does not exceed it. So I_B = 130A. The reasoning for every choice is arithmetically correct.

explanationIssues: The explanation says the 8m distance from breaker to outlet 'does not change the judgment' (判定を変えない). That is wrong as a reason. Article 149(2)(i)(c)(イ) and Table 149-2 relax the wire size when the run from a single outlet to the branch point is 3m or less. For a breaker over 20A up to 30A, the table allows 1.6mm. The 8m condition exists to rule out that relaxation. Without it, the 2.0mm wire in ロ could be argued acceptable. Suggested rewrite: 'The run from breaker to outlet is 8m, which is over 3m, so the Article 149(2)(i)(c)(イ) relaxation (Table 149-2) does not apply. Judge by Table 149-1 and Table 149-3.'
assessment.verifiedEvidence: Checked the official figure (20240526_co_second_q01.pdf, Q10) against official answer イ. The breaker ratings, wire sizes, and outlet ratings and counts for choices イ, ロ, ハ and ニ all match the original. The four crops q10-i/ro/ha/ni.png match. Legal basis: https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/safety_security/industrial_safety/sangyo/electric/files/20231226-2.pdf. WebFetch returned 403, so I used the attached SHA-pinned excerpt (PDF p.148-149). Article 149(1)(i) allows up to 3m. Table 149-1: breaker over 15A up to 20A needs 1.6mm; over 20A up to 30A needs 2.6mm. Table 149-3: breaker over 15A up to 20A allows outlets of 20A or less; over 20A up to 30A needs outlets from 20A to 30A. Article 149(2)(i)(c)(イ) and Table 149-2 give the 3m-or-less relaxation.

explanationIssues: The explanation says Table 146-3 'shows the upper temperature limit of 60℃' (その上限温度60℃を示している). This goes beyond what the text says. The table only gives the correction formula √((60−θ)/30) for 'vinyl compounds (excluding heat-resistant ones)'. It does not use the word '最高許容温度' (maximum permissible temperature) and does not name IV. Suggested rewrite: make official answer ロ the main basis, and describe Table 146-3 only as consistent. Its formula for non-heat-resistant vinyl compounds, √((60−θ)/30), drops to zero at 60℃ ambient.
sourceIssues: The cited source, https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/safety_security/industrial_safety/sangyo/electric/files/20231226-2.pdf (Table 146-3), does not directly state either key fact. It never says IV insulation is a 'vinyl compound (excluding heat-resistant ones)'. It never says the IV maximum permissible temperature is 60℃. I tried to confirm this in the METI commentary on the interpretation (https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/safety_security/industrial_safety/law/files/dengikaishakukaisetsu.pdf), but it returned 403, so I could not confirm it.

Checked the official figure (20240526_co_second_q01.pdf, Q19) against official answer ロ. The table rows a–d (wires / ring sleeve / crimp mark) match the original, and the q19.png crop matches. Technical basis: the exam center's official resource https://www.shiken.or.jp/construction/upload/point2024.pdf, p.22, 'Ring sleeve (E type) and wire combinations (per JIS C 2806)', via the attached SHA-pinned excerpt. Same size: 1.6mm × 2 is small with the ○ mark; 1.6mm × 3–4 is small with the small mark. Mixed sizes: 2.0mm × 1 + 1.6mm × 1–2 is small/small; 2.0mm × 2 + 1.6mm × 1–3 is medium/medium. So a and d are correct and b and c are wrong, which gives ロ.

Checked the official figure (20240526_co_second_q01.pdf, Q22) against official answer ロ. The question text, a–d, and the choices match the original. Legal basis: https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/safety_security/industrial_safety/sangyo/electric/files/20231226-2.pdf. WebFetch returned 403, so I used the attached SHA-pinned excerpt (PDF p.164). Article 167(2): when low-voltage wiring installed by cable work comes near or crosses weak-current wires, it must be installed so the two do not touch. c (10cm clearance) and d (a sturdy barrier) avoid contact and are correct. a and b are in contact and are wrong.
